item.title: Hisatsune chips in for birdie after water ball, shoots 63 to take 2nd-round lead at Phoenix Open
item.description: Ryo Hisatsune turned a water ball into a birdie to electrify the juiced up crowds at the Phoenix Open. The post Hisatsune chips in for birdie after water ball, shoots 63 to take 2nd-round lead at Phoenix Open appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: Patrick Reed takes the lead in Qatar and tries to wrap up Middle East swing with another win
item.description: Patrick Reed birdied two of his last three holes Friday for a 5-under 67, giving him a one-shot lead in the Qatar Masters as the American tries to wrap up a career-changing month in the Middle East with another victory. The post Patrick Reed takes the lead in Qatar and tries to wrap up Middle East swing with another win appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: Letter to the editor
item.description: Letter write voices concerns about the data centers in Columbia County. The post Letter to the editor appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: Augusta teens, 13 and 14, arrested in vehicle break-ins, stolen gun recovered
item.description: Two juveniles, ages 13 and 14, were arrested Thursday night in Richmond County after investigators caught them trying to break into vehicles, one of them armed with a stolen gun, according to the Richmond County Sheriff’s Office. The post Augusta teens, 13 and 14, arrested in vehicle break-ins, stolen gun recovered appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: Columbia County woman gets nearly six years in federal prison for stolen-check fraud scheme
item.description: A Columbia County woman was sentenced Thursday to 70 months in federal prison for using fake and stolen checks to commit bank fraud and aggravated identity theft. The post Columbia County woman gets nearly six years in federal prison for stolen-check fraud scheme appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: Warrant confirms: Josey High principal accused of pulling assistant principal by hair
item.description: Newly-released court documents allege that Dr. Derrias Priestley, principal of T.W. Josey High School, grabbed an assistant principal by the hair and dragged her down a school hallway, conduct that led to a simple battery charge this week, nearly nine months after the incident allegedly occurred. The post Warrant confirms: Josey High principal accused of pulling assistant principal by hair appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: Overwhelming vote backs efforts to investigate campaign money pumped into Georgia
item.description: Millions of dollars of out-of-state campaign money flowing into Georgia could soon be more strongly policed in the wake of mysterious political TV ads and big spending on recent elections. The post Overwhelming vote backs efforts to investigate campaign money pumped into Georgia appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: Jason Mraz bringing “Still Yours” tour to Columbia County Performing Arts Center
item.description: Multi-platinum, multi-GRAMMY Award-winning artist Jason Mraz has announced “Still Yours,” an East Coast tour running in May and June, with a stop scheduled in Evans. The post Jason Mraz bringing “Still Yours” tour to Columbia County Performing Arts Center appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: Richmond County school board reschedules Josey public hearings, delays master plan vote
item.description: The Richmond County Board of Education has rescheduled public hearings related to the district’s master plan following recent weather-related schedule changes and has moved its final vote to Feb. 23, according to an open letter signed by board president Shawnda Stovall. The post Richmond County school board reschedules Josey public hearings, delays master plan vote appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: Charter review panel sets hiring for Augusta attorney, clerk; debates pace of work
item.description: Augusta’s Charter Review Committee approved draft charter language Thursday defining how the city would fill two positions called the Augusta attorney and Augusta clerk. The post Charter review panel sets hiring for Augusta attorney, clerk; debates pace of work appeared first on The Augusta Press.
